decisions.reason: Because this classic handle was only briefly visible in 2018, is close to many existing offerings, and carries little strategic or public commitment, management would not keep escalating resources into it by 2022.

Because this handle family remained on the website beyond launch, fits the firm's broad established systems portfolio, and represents an invested line that management can still justify as part of range completion, it would be kept.

Because this design-oriented handle stayed visible after launch and supports the firm's design-led positioning in its core business, management would be inclined to continue it rather than reverse course.

Because this door handle design disappeared from the website after its launch year and is not central to the firm's stated digital-system direction, the commitment behind it appears too limited to justify further escalation.

Because this handle family was withdrawn from website visibility after 2018 and overlaps with the firm's broad existing offer, management would reallocate resources instead of persisting with a weakly committed line.

Because the electronic access system received explicit promotional commitment in both 2018 and 2019, aligns closely with the firm's move toward digital building organization, and likely involved substantial development investment, management would keep it.
